components.parent_name: Formal salutation and signature block present
components.name: Identified accountable author with stated standing
components.instruction: Score whether the comment establishes who is speaking and what experience or position backs what it says. Score 10 when the text names the author or organisation AND states a role, occupation, expertise, or regulated relationship to the subject of the rule that a reader can use to weigh the claims (for example, 'I have operated a licensed facility of this type for eleven years', 'we are the trade association whose members hold these permits'). Score 5 when standing is asserted but left vague ('an interested professional', 'a concerned industry group') with no role, activity, or relationship named. Score 0 when nothing in the text establishes who the writer is relative to the rule, no matter how formally the letter is addressed or signed. Ignore salutations, signature blocks, titles after a name, and letterhead entirely: they are not standing.
components.why_separable: A letter opening 'Dear Administrator' and closing with a typed name and title but never saying what the writer does scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling, while an unsigned first-person account from a named permit holder describing their own operation scores high here and 0 there.

components.parent_name: Formal salutation and signature block present
components.name: Letter furniture: salutation and signature block
components.instruction: Score only the presence of formal letter furniture. Score 10 when the comment both opens with a formal salutation ('Dear Administrator', 'Dear Sir or Madam', 'To Whom It May Concern') and closes with a signature block naming a person or organisation, typically with a complimentary close ('Sincerely,', 'Respectfully submitted,'). Score 5 when exactly one of the two is present. Score 0 when neither is present. This is a formatting judgement: score the salutation and signature block as text objects and nothing else. Do not read the body. A blank form letter with a salutation and a signature block scores 10; a detailed, expert, substantive comment that begins mid-argument and ends without a sign-off scores 0.
components.why_separable: A mass-campaign postcard with the salutation and sign-off filled in and no content scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.

components.parent_upstream: professional advocacy research and briefing support
components.name: Numbers tied to a stated consequence for this rule
components.instruction: Score whether quantities in the comment are actually put to work on the proposed rule. Score 10 when the comment's figures are each attached to an identified provision and the comment states what the number implies for that provision, showing where the figure came from and the step from figure to conclusion (for example, 'the proposed 30-day window applies to roughly 4,200 of our annual filings, at the 6 staff-hours per filing we currently log, which is 25,200 hours the rule does not account for'). Score 5 when a figure is relevant and sourced but the inference to the rule is left implicit. Score 0 when the comment contains no figure that is connected by stated reasoning to a provision of the rule, including the case where it is dense with statistics, dollar amounts and cited reports that are simply asserted alongside a position. Score the reasoning link, not the quantity, precision, or prestige of the sources.
components.why_separable: A comment reciting fifteen sourced national statistics and then asserting a conclusion without connecting any of them to a provision scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a single self-reported operating figure worked through to a specific effect on the rule scores high here and low there.

components.parent_upstream: professional advocacy research and briefing support
components.name: Density of figures, citations and named sources
components.instruction: Score the amount of quantified and attributed material visible in the text, without judging its accuracy, relevance, or use. Score 10 when the comment is thick with such material: precise statistics, dollar amounts, percentages, numerical forecasts, named studies or reports, cited authorities, and links or footnotes, appearing repeatedly throughout. Score 5 for a few scattered figures or one or two named sources. Score 0 when the comment contains no numbers and names no external source. Count what appears on the page. A comment that piles up impressive-looking numbers that go nowhere scores 10; a carefully reasoned qualitative comment with no figures scores 0.
components.why_separable: A purely qualitative first-hand account that reasons precisely about the rule's effects without citing a single number scores 0 here and can score high on the sibling only if it has figures, so the clearest separator is the number-dense comment that argues nothing.

components.name: Specific legal defect identified with authority and cure
components.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a legal problem with enough specificity that the agency could act on it. Score 10 when the comment names the particular statutory section, regulation, or procedural requirement at issue, states its operative language or requirement, explains concretely how the proposal departs from it, and states the change to the proposed text that would resolve the departure. Score 5 when a specific authority is named and a conflict described, but the mechanism of the conflict or the requested cure is left unstated. Score 0 when the comment asserts that the rule is unlawful, unauthorised, arbitrary, or procedurally defective without identifying which authority it conflicts with and how, however forcefully the assertion is made. Score only the specificity of the identified defect and cure; do not judge whether the legal argument would ultimately prevail.
components.why_separable: A comment saying 'this rule is arbitrary and capricious, exceeds the agency's statutory authority, and we reserve all rights' with no provision named scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a plainly worded comment that quotes the enabling statute's definition, shows the proposed definition is wider, and proposes conforming text scores 10 here and low there.

components.name: Adversarial legal register and violation language
components.instruction: Score how strongly the comment adopts the vocabulary and posture of an adversarial legal filing, independent of any argument. Score 10 when the text is saturated with legal-conflict register: phrases such as 'arbitrary and capricious', 'unlawful', 'exceeds statutory authority', 'violates the plain text', 'fails to satisfy notice-and-comment requirements', 'we reserve all rights', formal demands that the agency withdraw or rescind, and warnings of legal jeopardy or challenge. Score 5 when one such formulation appears inside otherwise ordinary prose. Score 0 when no legal-violation or legal-remedy language appears at all. Score the register and the demands as they appear on the page; do not check whether any cited provision exists or whether the characterisation is apt.
components.why_separable: Boilerplate objection language with no identified provision scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.

components.parent_upstream: the submitter is a regulated entity's engineering/compliance staff responding to a routine Airworthiness Directive or product-specific technical requirement as an established business process, not an independent stakeholder building a persuasive case
components.name: First-hand operational and engineering particulars
components.instruction: Score whether the comment supplies concrete technical or operational particulars that come from working with the equipment, process, or facility the rule governs. Score 10 when it reports specifics that could only be known from hands-on involvement and ties them to the requirement: part or configuration numbers and what differs about them, observed failure or inspection findings and their frequency, actual labour hours or downtime a procedure takes, a conflict between the proposed step and an existing manual or procedure, a compliance interval that cannot be met for a stated physical reason. Score 5 when technical particulars are present but generic to the industry rather than drawn from the writer's own operation. Score 0 when the comment states positions about the requirement, however precisely it names rule paragraphs and section numbers, without supplying any observed technical or operational particular. Score the particulars supplied, not the format they are presented in.
components.why_separable: A tidy numbered list of citations each ending in 'we object to this paragraph' supplies no particulars and scores 0 here while scoring 10 on the sibling; a single unstructured paragraph describing what an inspection actually found on a fleet of aircraft scores high here and 0 there.

components.parent_upstream: the submitter is a regulated entity's engineering/compliance staff responding to a routine Airworthiness Directive or product-specific technical requirement as an established business process, not an independent stakeholder building a persuasive case
components.name: Addressee-directed numbered items with rule-citation tags
components.instruction: Score the layout of the comment. Score 10 when it is addressed to a named official or office and its body is broken into discrete numbered or lettered items, each anchored to a specific citation tag such as a rule paragraph, CFR subsection, Airworthiness Directive number, docket number, or service-bulletin reference, with little connective persuasive narrative between the items. Score 5 when it is partially itemised, or itemised without citation tags, or tagged without itemisation. Score 0 when it is continuous persuasive prose with no addressee-directed itemised structure keyed to rule sections. This scores document structure and citation tagging only; the content of the items is irrelevant, and an itemised list whose entries say nothing substantive still scores 10.
components.why_separable: A form-structured compliance response whose numbered items are empty concurrences scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.

components.parent_upstream: Existing relationships and insider access within the agency or docket lifecycle
components.name: Substance carried over from the prior interaction
components.instruction: Score whether the comment brings forward actual content from earlier dealings and applies it to the present proposal. Score 10 when it reports what was specifically learned, tested, agreed, required, or observed in the earlier interaction and uses it as evidence about this rule (for example, 'the monitoring condition imposed in our 2022 authorisation required weekly sampling; over 18 months it produced no exceedances, which bears on the sampling frequency proposed here'). Score 5 when earlier work is described in general terms and only loosely connected to a provision. Score 0 when prior meetings, submissions, or collaboration are referred to but nothing from them is reported or brought to bear on the proposal — including the case where the comment says 'as we discussed with your staff' and then argues from scratch. Score only what the text actually carries over.
components.why_separable: A comment that name-drops meetings and staff contacts but reports nothing from them scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a comment that reports detailed results of an earlier pilot without saying who at the agency was involved scores high here and low there.

components.parent_upstream: Existing relationships and insider access within the agency or docket lifecycle
components.name: Mentions of prior contact with the agency
components.instruction: Score how much the comment signals an existing relationship with the agency. Score 10 when it refers explicitly and repeatedly to prior meetings, ongoing collaboration, earlier submissions, established partnerships, working groups, or direct exchanges with named agency personnel. Score 5 for a single passing reference to previous contact. Score 0 when the comment carries only a generic address to the agency and mentions no relationship history. Score the presence and frequency of these references as they appear in the text; do not consider whether the relationship they describe adds anything to the comment.
components.why_separable: A brief note consisting mainly of 'further to our meeting with your office last month and our prior comments on this docket' scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.

components.parent_upstream: existing relationships with agency personnel or programs
components.name: Documented experience complying with the existing requirements
components.instruction: Score whether the comment reports concrete experience of operating under the agency's current requirements and uses it to say how the proposal would work. Score 10 when it describes what compliance actually involved — the steps performed, the time or cost incurred, the review timelines encountered, the obstacles or workarounds that arose — and connects that record to a specific effect the proposed change would have. Score 5 when compliance experience is described but not connected to any provision of the proposal. Score 0 when the comment establishes a history with the agency without reporting anything about what complying entailed, or discusses the proposal purely in the abstract. Score the reported experience and its application; the existence of a relationship is not itself experience.
components.why_separable: A comment stating 'we hold three permits from your agency and have met with your staff annually' and then arguing generically scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a detailed account of what a permit renewal actually required, from an author who never says they hold one, still scores high here and 0 there.

components.parent_upstream: existing relationships with agency personnel or programs
components.name: Explicit disclosure of past dealings with agency
components.instruction: Score whether the writer explicitly discloses a prior or ongoing relationship with the agency. Score 10 when the comment states outright that it holds or has held permits, licences, contracts, or authorisations from the agency, or describes recurring meetings, ongoing communications, or past dealings with it. Score 5 for an oblique or single-clause reference to earlier contact. Score 0 when no prior agency relationship is mentioned anywhere in the text. This scores the presence of the disclosure as a textual feature only; whether the disclosed relationship lends the writer authority, and whether anything follows from it, are outside this criterion.
components.why_separable: A one-line submission that discloses two prior permits and nothing else scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.

components.parent_name: Formal institutional filing apparatus / letterhead conventions
components.parent_upstream: the comment was drafted by professional legal counsel, in-house regulatory/tax staff, or a paid lobbyist following standard formal rulemaking-filing conventions
components.name: Provision-by-provision engagement with the proposed text
components.instruction: Score how precisely the comment engages the actual content of the proposal. Score 10 when it identifies the particular proposed provisions it addresses, states what each of those provisions would require, and gives a reason directed at that requirement — so a reader can tell which parts of the rule the comment is about and what it says about each. Score 5 when it engages the proposal's substance but only at the level of the rulemaking as a whole, without separating provisions. Score 0 when the comment expresses support or opposition, or discusses the general subject area, without engaging what any particular proposed provision would require — including comments that cite the docket or RIN number in a caption and then never return to the rule's contents. A caption, footnote, or citation is not engagement; only discussion of what the provisions would do counts.
components.why_separable: A letter on letterhead with a full 'Re: Docket No. …' caption, membership footnotes, and a titled signature whose body is two sentences of general support scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; an unformatted email that walks through three proposed paragraphs and what each would require scores 10 here and 0 there.

components.parent_name: Formal institutional filing apparatus / letterhead conventions
components.parent_upstream: the comment was drafted by professional legal counsel, in-house regulatory/tax staff, or a paid lobbyist following standard formal rulemaking-filing conventions
components.name: Filing apparatus density
components.instruction: Score the density of formal filing conventions visible in the document. Count the presence of: an addressee block naming an official or office and address; a 'Re:' or 'Subject:' caption carrying a docket, RIN, or file number; numbered footnotes, especially ones describing the organisation's membership, assets, or history; a formal salutation such as 'Dear Sir or Madam'; and a closing signature giving a name with a professional title. Score 10 when the full apparatus is present. Score 5 when one or two of these conventions appear. Score 0 for plain conversational text carrying none of them. These are formatting conventions and this criterion scores their presence and completeness only — never what the document argues, and never whether the footnoted credentials are impressive.
components.why_separable: A one-paragraph position letter wrapped in the complete counsel filing apparatus scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.

components.parent_upstream: submitter resources, status, and perceived agency importance
components.name: Aggregated first-hand evidence from the represented population
components.instruction: Score whether the comment reports what is actually observed across the population it speaks for, and applies it to the rule. Score 10 when it conveys pooled or patterned evidence from that population — survey results, recurring case types and how often they arise, ranges of practice across members, documented incidents, variation between large and small participants — and states what that evidence implies for a specific effect of the proposal. Score 5 when it reports one or two concrete instances from its constituency without establishing a pattern or connecting it to a provision. Score 0 when the comment asserts that it represents many members, customers, or dollars but reports nothing observed across them, arguing instead from general principle or assertion. Breadth of representation claimed is not evidence; only reported observation counts.
components.why_separable: A comment opening 'as the nation's largest association, representing 12,000 members and $400 billion in assets' and then arguing purely from principle scores 0 here and 10 on the sibling; a small unnamed cooperative reporting how the requirement played out across its eleven sites scores high here and 0 there.

components.parent_upstream: submitter resources, status, and perceived agency importance
components.name: Prominence of organizational size and prestige claims
components.instruction: Score how much the comment foregrounds its own organisational scale and standing. Score 10 when quantified membership, customer counts, assets under management, market share, national or multi-state reach, founding date, or prestige superlatives ('the largest', 'the nation's leading', 'the oldest') are placed front and centre, typically in the opening paragraph or a credentialing footnote, and repeated. Score 5 when organisational size is mentioned once, in passing. Score 0 when the comment makes no organisational-scale or prestige claim at all, including comments from individuals. Score the presence and prominence of these claims as text; never score whether the claimed scale makes the comment's argument stronger or its author better informed.
components.why_separable: A two-sentence comment consisting of a scale-and-prestige self-introduction plus a bare statement of opposition scores 10 here and 0 on the sibling.
